label: The parent packet reports that import time remained 302 seconds after the core lane stopped collecting the deep-loop suite; the updated core run collected 126 spec-kit files and the config check recorded 129 collected files. The persistent cost therefore is not explained by importing the excluded deep-loop suite. The core Vitest config runs files in parallel, with each file in its own worker process; the shared setup allocates a scratch database per test file and removes it afterward. Repeated worker setup and module initialization across the 129-file core lane are plausible contributors, but the available sources do not measure their import share. The runner times the whole Vitest invocation and logs one elapsed total; it exposes no stage- or module-level import timer in the inspected path. The sharded runner starts each shard as a separate process sequentially to address accumulated worker CPU rehashing, so it is not evidence of lower import time or wall time.
